cards.text: Friend, the Jews are in danger: Haman has promised money to the king's treasury to destroy them, and Mordecai has told Queen Esther to go to the king and plead with him for her people. Problem is, walking in on the king without being summoned can get you put to death, and she hasn't been called in thirty days. So the Jews in Susa fast, Esther fasts with them, and she says, "And if I perish, I perish!"

On the third day, Esther puts on her royal robes and stands in the inner court, right across from the king's quarters. The king is on his throne, facing the entrance, so there is NO sneaking in on this man.

cards.question: As soon as the king sees Esther standing in the court uninvited, she finds favor in his sight.
The king holds out the gold ___ in his hand toward Esther, and she comes forward and touches its tip.

cards.text: She's still standing, friend. Everybody breathe. Then the king asks, "What is it, Queen Esther?" and he makes her an offer.

cards.question: The king asks Esther what her request is. How much is he willing to give her?
With up to half the kingdom on the table, what does Esther ask the king for?

answers.text: The king and Haman at her banquet today
An end to the law against the Jews
A pardon for Mordecai at the gate

cards.question: When Esther invites them to her banquet, the king says there's no rush to bring Haman.

cards.text: So the king and Haman go to the banquet Esther prepared. As they drink their wine, the king asks her again what her petition is.

cards.question: At the banquet, the king once again offers Esther up to half the kingdom.
The king asks Esther again what she wants. What does she answer him?

answers.text: Come back tomorrow for another banquet
Cancel the law against the Jews
Send Haman away from the palace

cards.text: Tomorrow, she says. Then she'll answer the king's question. That's like texting somebody "I've got something to tell you" and then "tell you tomorrow." NOBODY sleeps easy after that text.
That day Haman walks out full of joy and glad of heart. Then he gets to the king's gate, and there's Mordecai.

cards.question: Haman walks past Mordecai at the king's gate. What does Mordecai do?

answers.text: He bows down to the ground
He gets up and walks away

cards.question: Seeing Mordecai at the gate, Haman goes from glad of heart to being filled with ___ toward Mordecai.
Haman lets his rage out on Mordecai right there at the king's gate.

cards.text: Haman holds it together, goes home and calls in his friends and his wife Zeresh. Then he reads them his own highlight reel: his glorious wealth, his many sons, and every way the king has honored and promoted him.

cards.question: Then Haman adds one more brag to the list. What is it?

answers.text: Only he was invited to Esther's banquet
The king named him governor of Susa
Esther asked him for his advice

cards.question: After all that bragging, Haman says none of it satisfies him as long as he sees ___ sitting at the king's gate.

cards.text: So his wife Zeresh and all his friends speak up. They've got advice for him.

cards.question: What do Zeresh and Haman's friends tell him to have built?

answers.text: A prison next to the gate
A tower over the city wall

cards.question: Zeresh and his friends tell Haman to ask the king in the morning to have Mordecai hanged. The advice pleases Haman, and he has the gallows built.

cards.text: Last step of their advice: go to the banquet with the king and enjoy himself. We'll leave it right there, friend, because this story is a long way from done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "tell you tomorrow.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Haman and Mordecai first show up in this lesson on the opening card, but neither is introduced. The baker isn't told that Haman is the king's top official or that Mordecai is Esther's cousin. Haman's 'Only he was invited' brag and his rage at Mordecai depend on knowing who these two are.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Only he was invited to Esther's banquet', says something the text shows is wrong. Esther 5:4 and 5:12 show the king was invited too. Haman's brag is that Esther 'invited no one but me to join the king.' A wording like 'Only he joined the king at Esther's banquet' keeps it true.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Card 10 already tells the baker the advice pleased Haman and he had the gallows built, the end of Esther 5:14. Card 11 then goes back to an earlier part of the same verse, the advice to go to the banquet and enjoy himself. The last story card steps backward through the passage instead of forward. The 'enjoy yourself' part of the advice should come before the outcome, for example on card 8 or folded into card 10's setup.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has almost no real laughs. Cards 1 and 8 are plain retelling, and card 5's 'highlight reel' is only mildly amusing. This stretch is a natural comic moment that can hold a laugh without muddying any facts: Haman goes from full of joy to full of rage, lists all his wealth, sons and honors, then says none of it satisfies him because one man won't stand up. The lines read like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
